rules.title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance (2026 inflation-adjusted amounts)
rules.requirement: If your Berkeley landlord evicts you for an owner move-in, they must pay relocation assistance. From January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, plus an extra $6,471 for qualifying households.
rules.key_value: $19,413 standard; additional $6,471 for qualifying households (effective 2026-01-01; 1.5% CPI adjustment)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley rental units covered by the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance who are evicted for owner move-in. Amounts are indexed to the CPI-U for the San Francisco-Oakland-San Jose region and published every year by the Rent Board.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance (Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76)
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.

rules.title: Ellis Act withdrawal relocation assistance (2026 inflation-adjusted amounts)
rules.requirement: If your Berkeley landlord evicts you to take the property off the rental market under the Ellis Act, they must pay relocation assistance. From January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, plus an extra $6,471 for qualifying households.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley who are evicted because the owner is removing the property from the rental housing market under the Ellis Act. Amounts are indexed to inflation every year.
rules.citation: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance (Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.77)
rules.quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.

notes: The document is an official Berkeley Rent Board news item. It does not give code section numbers. The Berkeley Municipal Code chapter numbers in the citations (13.76 and 13.77) come from general knowledge, not from this document, so check them. The dollar amounts and the 2026-01-01 effective date appear in the document, but each sits on its own line and cannot be quoted together in one span with the sentence around it. So the quoted spans use the sentences that describe each ordinance's relocation requirement. The page does not give eligibility criteria for the additional payment for qualifying households, or any coverage exemptions. Ellis Act relocation sits within limits set by the state Ellis Act (Gov. Code § 7060 et seq.), which allows local relocation assistance requirements. This document does not mention that.
